decisions.reason: After remaining on the market beyond launch and given its close fit with the firm's core space-camera business, management would likely see its performance as at least near aspiration and keep it.
As a modular camera line with several models and strong strategic fit, Product B signals commitment and likely satisfactory results relative to aspirations, so it would be kept.

Because this sensor suite extends established capabilities into a related market and the firm has organizational slack in a growing R&D-intensive industry, management would likely continue it unless clearer underperformance appeared.

Its more tentative market presentation keeps review pressure relatively high, but its relevance to miniaturized space sensing and the firm's tolerance for uncertain adjacent products make retention still more likely than withdrawal.

As a newly launched radiation-hard camera line with several models and a dedicated page, Product E reflects a meaningful commitment that management would normally support through the early uncertain phase.

Although the asteroid navigation camera appears more exploratory and was only mentioned rather than strongly showcased, its technological relatedness and the long commercial cycles in space markets make a near-term drop less likely than continued patience.
